record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.context_brief: Circular-arc graphs in H-free graph classes
record.original_question: For every four-vertex graph H, characterize by forbidden induced subgraphs the circular-arc graphs within the class of H-free graphs. In this question, an H-free graph means a graph containing no induced subgraph isomorphic to H, and a circular-arc graph means an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle. The requested characterization should identify the induced obstructions that exactly separate circular-arc graphs from non-circular-arc graphs under the assumption that H is absent as an induced subgraph.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs within the class of H-free graphs where H is a four-vertex graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A circular-arc graph is the intersection graph of a family of open arcs on a circle: vertices correspond to arcs, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding arcs intersect. For a fixed graph H, a graph G is called H-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to H.

Problem: For every graph H on four vertices, determine a characterization, by a (finite or explicit) list of forbidden induced subgraphs, of the circular-arc graphs that lie in the class of H-free graphs. In other words, for each such H, exhibit the family F_H of graphs such that, for every H-free graph G, G is a circular-arc graph if and only if G contains no induced subgraph from F_H.
artifact.status_search_result: A general forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circular-arc graphs remains a long-standing open problem. Characterizations exist for some restricted subclasses (e.g., Helly circular-arc graphs, normal Helly circular-arc graphs) and within particular H-free classes such as split graphs (Cao et al., 2024). However, a complete case-by-case resolution for every four-vertex H does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Circular-arc Graphs: I. Split Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Finding a forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circular-arc graphs is a long-standing open problem; we provide one within the class of split graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result for one specific four-vertex H (K_1+K_3, giving split graphs).

status_evidence.title: Locally interval graphs are circular-arc graphs
status_evidence.claim: Related subclass results exist but no full four-vertex H classification.
